payload.name: Preserve source or discovery details in extraction
payload.description: When extracting memories from a user message, if the message states how a person heard about or discovered an event, keep that detail in a memory.
content: When building memory candidates from a message, treat how the person learned about or discovered an event (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, read an ad) as a durable fact. Include it in the event memory or create a separate memory for it, even when the main action is something else. Do not drop this detail during extraction or later updates.

solves: During extraction, when a message states how the person learned about or discovered an event (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, read an ad), that detail is often omitted when the main action is captured, so later questions like "how did X hear about Y?" cannot be answered. Preserving source/discovery details as part of the event memory or as a separate memory generalizes across workshops, classes, sales, and announcements; it does not require storing transient or non-durable context.
